messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT triggered: us-west-2a inference path — elevated 5xx + token timeouts. alert rule: inference.errors.count > 50 in 5m. Pager: @alex.k

alex.k: I’m oncall, ack. seeing spike in 504s for hosted API routes hitting g5 pool in us-west-2a. marking SEV-2 for now.

priya.m: noticed a sharp rise in TCP retransmits and socket backlog on the node metrics. ENI tx queue length trending up on several pods. clients seeing partial responses / stalls.

josh.s: route health checks show NLB target failures intermittently — connection resets from instances, not the NLB itself. Could be kernel network stack getting saturated, or driver backpressure.

alex.k: creating mitigation plan: 1) divert new traffic away from us-west-2a for eligible models 2) spin up additional warm instances in us-west-2b and us-east-1 to absorb load 3) enable faster DNS failover / weighted routing for read paths.

sre-backups: @alex.k I’ll coordinate traffic steering. preparing route53 change with low TTL but will rely on our control-plane routing first.

deployment-bot: Deploy job started: routing-proxy:v3.14 -> canary in us-west-2b.

priya.m: quick data: kernel drop counters (per-host):
```
host-12: tx_queue=2400, drops=1200
host-13: tx_queue=1900, drops=850
host-14: tx_queue=3000, drops=1700
```
These correlate with per-request latency spikes at the runtime layer (KV cache stalls).

josh.s: I’m initiating targeted draining of unhealthy G5s in us-west-2a to force routing off those nodes. enabling connection drain on NLB targets for 300s.

cs-lead-bot: Notifying impacted customers with id list: CUST-9821, CUST-1102, CUST-5015 (partial 504/timeout symptoms). ETA for official CS note: 15m.

alex.k: mitigation step executed: control-plane rerouted ~33% of inference traffic to us-west-2b immediately (models with multi-region pinning allowed). Observed drop in error-rate from 8% -> 3% in 7 minutes for routed models.

priya.m: started a live kernel parameter tweak on a subset of hosts (tcp_rmem/tcp_wmem, net.core.netdev_max_backlog) as an emergency measure — results stable on the test pool but still monitoring.

josh.s: scaling action: +6 warm g5 instances in us-west-2b, autoscaler bumped workers in us-east-1 by +8 to handle cross-region traffic.

alex.k: rolling checklist:
- [x] Traffic diversion to other AZs/regions (control-plane)
- [x] NLB draining for suspect targets
- [x] Warm capacity added in us-west-2b/us-east-1
- [x] Customers notified (CS team)
- [ ] Postmortem owner assigned (pending)

sre-backups: Route53 weighted routing change committed as secondary. TTL lowered to 30s for affected hostnames. Note: relying on our router for the main handoff to avoid DNS churn.

deployment-bot: canary succeeded in us-west-2b, promoting routing-proxy:v3.14 across regional fleet.

priya.m: after draining and kernel tweaks, dropped queue lengths on remaining us-west-2a hosts: tx_queue average down to ~400. Still seeing a small number of reconnects but much improved.

alex.k: current status: partial mitigation in place, majority of customer traffic successful. Impact: brief higher latency (200-800ms) and transient 504s for 10–30min window for some customers pinned to us-west-2a. No data loss.

josh.s: root cause hypothesis (working): NIC/driver or hypervisor-level packet scheduling issue under high concurrent ephemeral ENI usage causing TX queue backlog and connection resets. Not a GFE networking outage.

sre-backups: paging ops note: we should avoid mass instance reboots unless required. prefer draining + scaling + kernel params as we did.

cs-lead-bot: CS message posted to affected customers. Suggest follow-up with technical summary once we have RCA.

alex.k: oncall handoff in 40m to @josh.s — I’ll capture chronology and current mitigations into the incident tracker. Josh, you take POC for postmortem and RCA.

josh.s: acked. I’ll collect iostat, dmesg, ENI metrics, and packet captures for the suspected hosts. Will coordinate vendor support if any driver-level hints emerge.

priya.m: quick note — we observed one model that amplified connection fanout due to retry behavior. Recommend adding jittered backoff in the aggregator client to avoid amplifying load during degraded network conditions.

alex.k: post-incident next steps (owner assignments):
- RCA writeup: josh.s
- Kernel tuning playbook: priya.m
- Routing hardening + DNS policy: sre-backups
- Customer-facing summary: cs-lead-bot + alex.k
- Postmortem publish target: 72h

josh.s: leaving a final live marker: remaining minor errors at ~0.4% for us-west-2a, overall platform error-rate back to baseline. Will open a dedicated ticket for driver/instance lifecycle review.

sre-backups: closing incident channel for now, will re-open if regressions show. Thanks team. :tada:

deployment-bot: Incident status set -> resolved (post-mitigation).
